text:
Recent evidence supports testing diagnostic tools against seeded defects before trusting their explanations. A [2024 recommender study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infsof.2024.107410) evaluated six metamorphic relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise; applicability to sequential transformers still requires validation. A [2025 model-mutation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17638) warns that illegal mutations generate false positives. [DeepCrime](https://github.com/dlfaults/deepcrime) provides an earlier foundation: realistic fault operators, statistical comparisons, effect sizes and instability reporting. Its repeated-retraining protocol should not be copied into this fixed-checkpoint diagnostic exercise.

Suggested BERT4Rec adaptation: use temporary, isolated fixtures around each existing category model, injecting one defect at a time—visible masked targets, count-minus-one readout on left-padded sequences, disabled padding attention masks, incompatible checkpoint metadata, or incorrect category routing. Pair every mutation with an untouched control and verify that the fault actually activates. Check masked-target input construction directly; assert final-position readout for appended-mask inference; perturb masked padding embeddings while preserving positions; compare singleton versus batched predictions, candidate-permutation consistency and save/load score equivalence. Padding invariance requires preserving semantic position IDs. [Transformers documentation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/docs/source/en/troubleshooting.md) demonstrates silent output errors from unmasked padding.

Report detection as flagged activated faulty fixtures / all activated faulty fixtures, and false alarms as flagged clean fixtures / all clean fixtures, separately by defect and category. Record invalid, equivalent and unactivated mutations separately; distinguish explicit rejection from diagnostic localization. Set thresholds using clean controls, then freeze them before mutation evaluation. These are proposed checks, not measured results: the retrieved sources establish no detection rates for this toolkit. Successful fault detection also does not establish probability calibration or validate causal explanations of recommendation quality.
